transcript.text: Please note that if the electrics trip or you smell burning, stop using the dryer immediately, leave it switched off, and let me know. When the machine stops, observing the pattern of failure is very helpful for diagnosis. If you leave it to cool down for a while, will it start again and carry on, or not at all?
it doesnt break down, it finishes and says End but then the drum keeps turning every couple of minutes if I leave the clothes in. no burning smell
The type of dryer changes what to check. Is it a vented dryer (a hose out of the back), a condenser dryer with a water container, or a heat-pump dryer?
its a condenser, a Beko. I think it has a water container yes

Thanks for letting us know it’s a condenser model. Please switch off and unplug the dryer, and let it cool down first to ensure safety. A blocked filter can cause overheating, triggering a safety cut-out. Clean the fluff filter located in the door opening; note that some heat-pump models may have an additional filter at the bottom. The app shows a picture to help you locate this. Was it full of fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the lint filter is" — The fluff/lint filter sits in the door opening or just inside the rim. Lift it out and clear the fluff after every load. Typical layout — your dryer may differ.]
I haven't cleaned it yet. It does dry the clothes fine though, it's just the turning after End. Is that the filter?

Thanks for letting me know. No problem if you haven’t had a chance yet. A blocked filter makes the dryer overheat, and it then cuts out to protect itself. Clean the fluff filter in the door opening (heat-pump models often have a second filter at the bottom). Switch the dryer off, unplug it and let it cool down first. Was it full of fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
I haven't cleaned it yet, I'll go and do it now. But is that really why it keeps turning after End? It dries the clothes fine.

Thanks for letting us know about the lint filter status. Please switch the dryer off, unplug it and let it cool down first. Behind the flap at the bottom front there's a condenser unit (or a second filter on heat-pump models). Take it out and rinse the fluff off under the tap, then let it drip-dry and refit it. You can refer to the picture shown in the app for guidance. Was it clogged with fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the condenser and water tank are" — On a condenser dryer the water container pulls out at the top and the condenser/heat exchanger sits behind a flap at the bottom front — slide it out and rinse it. Condenser/heat-pump dryers only; layout may differ.]
